items.title: Phil Flanigan interviewed by Monk Rowe, San Diego, California, February 15, 1998
items.q: And then my dad told me about Scott LaFaro, who he knew very well... And he showed me the newspaper article... where LaFaro is on the cover

ctx.x: Clarinet, alto and tenor. And he worked with a bunch of guys around Geneva, around that Geneva, Canandaigua and Sampson Air Force Base, in the ‘50s when it was going, in a place called the Club 86 and the Holiday Bar and Grill in downtown Geneva. Club 86 had a lot of people through there: Coleman Hawkins, Dizzy and a bunch of people throughout the years. And I’ll mention to an older musician who I’ll meet from time to time, did you ever play a place called Club 86? And they go yeah, upstate New York, right? Yeah,…

they would go into Geneva and have parties and jam sessions and whatnot. But obviously the biggest jazz name out of my home town was Scott LaFaro. And I guess this isn’t really answering your question too good.
